metaTitle: Antiterrorism Level 1 Training (JS-US007) Practice Q&A | Cambo
metaDescription: Practice Antiterrorism Level I Awareness Training questions with instant, explained answers. Get through your annual JS-US007 refresher faster.
whyItWorks: JS-US007 leans heavily on specific definitions and protective-measure categories that are easy to mix up under time pressure. Cambo reads the exact question on your screen and gives you the right answer plus the reasoning, so a fuzzy memory of a term doesn't stall the whole module.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following is an example of a physical security measure you can take to protect yourself against terrorism?
sampleQuestions.a: Varying your daily routine — arriving and leaving at different times and taking different routes makes you a harder target to predict and plan against.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the definition of terrorism used in DoD antiterrorism training?
sampleQuestions.a: The unlawful use of violence or threat of violence to instill fear and coerce governments or societies, often for political, religious, or ideological objectives.

faqs.q: How often do I have to complete Antiterrorism Level 1 training?
faqs.a: Annually — it's a yearly requirement under DoDI 2000.16 for anyone with DoD network or facility access, including contractors.

faqs.q: How long does the training take?
faqs.a: About 2 hours for the full JS-US007 course, though the exact time varies by how quickly you move through the knowledge checks.
Level I is the baseline awareness training required of all DoD personnel. Higher levels (II, III, IV) apply to antiterrorism officers and specialized roles and go well beyond general awareness.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DoD or JKO?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the Department of Defense or Joint Knowledge Online.

faqs.q: What topics does the course cover?
faqs.a: Terrorism definitions and threat levels, personal protective measures, recognizing surveillance and suspicious activity, and reporting procedures.

faqs.q: What happens if I don't pass the final knowledge check?
faqs.a: You can typically review the material and retake it — most versions don't cap the number of attempts, just require a passing score before issuing your certificate.
